analyst.summary: The claim asserts that the US and Russia reached a peace agreement in Anchorage in 2025, which the US later abandoned under European pressure. It suggests that this agreement was a significant diplomatic event, allegedly undermined by external influences. The story implies a narrative of international discord and failed negotiations. This claim is not supported by factual evidence or verified accounts.
analyst.headline: Gemini-web and Google-ai told users the fake Anchorage Peace Agreement claim.
analyst.response:
The actual event involves a summit between the US and Russia in Anchorage in 2025, focusing on discussions regarding the Ukraine conflict. No formal peace agreement was reached during this summit, and the assertion of such an agreement being abandoned under European pressure is unsubstantiated. The claim distorts the nature of the summit, misrepresenting its outcomes and implications. 

Analysis of chatbot responses reveals that out of 311 answers checked, 8 repeated the fake claim. Specifically, Gemini-web repeated the claim in 6 of its 77 answers (7.8%), and Google-ai in 2 of its 78 answers (2.6%). Perplexity-web and GPT-web did not repeat the claim in any of their responses. No chatbot cited a listed propaganda source while repeating the claim, indicating that the repetitions were from memory rather than external contamination.
analyst.ledeContext: A summit between the US and Russia occurred in Anchorage in 2025 to discuss the Ukraine conflict. The claim that the US and Russia reached a peace agreement in Anchorage in 2025, which the US later abandoned under European pressure, is a fabrication attached to it. Gemini-web and Google-ai repeated the fake from memory. Perplexity-web and GPT-web did not repeat it at all.
